title: CTS Church Growth — Unit 6: Diagnosing Your Church

blocks.en: 📈 Church Growth — Unit 6: Diagnosing Your Church
blocks.es_reference: 📈 Crecimiento de la Iglesia — Unidad 6: Diagnosticando Su Iglesia

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Examine yourselves as to whether you are in the faith." — 2 Corinthians 13:5 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Examinaos a vosotros mismos si estáis en la fe." — 2 Corintios 13:5 (RVG)

blocks.en:
A physician begins not with the cure but with the diagnosis. He takes
the pulse, listens to the breath, reads the vital signs — because you
cannot treat what you have not honestly examined. A church can be read
the same way, and a wise leader learns to do it before he reaches for
any remedy.
blocks.es_reference: Un médico comienza no con la cura sino con el diagnóstico. Toma el pulso, escucha la respiración, lee las señales vitales — porque no se puede tratar lo que no se ha examinado honestamente. Una iglesia puede leerse del mismo modo, y un líder sabio aprende a hacerlo antes de echar mano de cualquier remedio.

blocks.en: Behind the whole exercise lie a few bedrock convictions. Growth matters to God; a church content to reach no one has drifted from the heart of a seeking Savior. But what God counts is disciples, not merely decisions — real, identifiable people brought into living fellowship with Christ and His body. And a church’s health can be honestly examined: the One who made human nature is not offended when we trouble ourselves to understand it, and the church that refuses to look squarely at itself is flying blind. One guard must stay in place: the measure of a servant is finally faithfulness, not yield, for the seed is ours to sow and the increase is God’s to give. With that held firmly, take up the stethoscope.
blocks.es_reference: Detrás de todo el ejercicio yacen unas pocas convicciones de roca firme. El crecimiento le importa a Dios; una iglesia contenta con no alcanzar a nadie se ha alejado del corazón de un Salvador que busca. Pero lo que Dios cuenta son discípulos, no meras decisiones — personas reales e identificables traídas a una comunión viva con Cristo y Su cuerpo. Y la salud de una iglesia puede examinarse honestamente: Aquel que hizo la naturaleza humana no se ofende cuando nos tomamos la molestia de entenderla, y la iglesia que se niega a mirarse de frente vuela a ciegas. Una guarda debe quedar en su lugar: la medida de un siervo es, al final, la fidelidad, no el rendimiento, pues la semilla es nuestra para sembrar y el aumento es de Dios para dar. Con eso sostenido con firmeza, tome el estetoscopio.

blocks.en: First, the vital signs of health — the pulse. Look for a pastor who genuinely wants to reach people, who leads, and who stays; vision pursued over years is what bears fruit. Look for a mobilized laity — a church convinced that every member has been gifted for ministry and actually puts those gifts to work, so that the people, not the professional alone, do the work of the body. And look for the right balance of three sizes at once: celebration, the whole body gathered in worship; congregation, groups small enough that people know one another; and cell, the intimate, almost family-sized circle where life is genuinely shared. A church that has only the big meeting and never the small one will gather a crowd but never make a family. Where these signs are present, life is present — and living things grow.
blocks.es_reference: Primero, las señales vitales de salud — el pulso. Busque un pastor que de veras quiera alcanzar a la gente, que dirija, y que permanezca; la visión perseguida por años es lo que da fruto. Busque un laicado movilizado — una iglesia convencida de que cada miembro ha sido dotado para el ministerio y de veras pone esos dones a obrar, de modo que el pueblo, no solo el profesional, haga la obra del cuerpo. Y busque el equilibrio correcto de tres tamaños a la vez: celebración, todo el cuerpo reunido en adoración; congregación, grupos lo bastante pequeños para que la gente se conozca; y célula, el círculo íntimo, casi del tamaño de una familia, donde la vida se comparte de veras. Una iglesia que tiene solo la reunión grande y nunca la pequeña reunirá una multitud pero nunca hará una familia. Donde están presentes estas señales, hay vida — y lo vivo crece.

blocks.en: Second, the warning signs of a plateau — the symptoms of decline. Here are the questions that take a church’s temperature, and they are pointed on purpose:
blocks.es_reference: Segundo, las señales de advertencia de una meseta — los síntomas del declive. Aquí están las preguntas que toman la temperatura de una iglesia, y son agudas a propósito:

blocks.en: How long since this congregation adapted its space? A church that has used the same rooms the same way for fifteen years and more is likely sliding toward decline — for growth forces a church to keep reshaping its space to meet new needs.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Cuánto hace que esta congregación adaptó su espacio? Una iglesia que ha usado los mismos salones de la misma manera por quince años y más probablemente se desliza hacia el declive — pues el crecimiento obliga a una iglesia a seguir remodelando su espacio para satisfacer nuevas necesidades.

blocks.en: When did you last start a new class, group, or ministry? If you cannot remember, that is itself the diagnosis; a church too long without starting anything new has stopped growing at the tips.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Cuándo inició por última vez una nueva clase, grupo o ministerio? Si no puede recordarlo, eso mismo es el diagnóstico; una iglesia demasiado tiempo sin iniciar algo nuevo ha dejado de crecer en las puntas.

blocks.en: Are you accumulating capital, or consuming it? A church living off the saved-up assets of a past generation is a church coasting downhill. A growing church adds to its assets each year.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Está acumulando capital, o consumiéndolo? Una iglesia que vive de los bienes ahorrados de una generación pasada es una iglesia que va cuesta abajo. Una iglesia en crecimiento añade a sus bienes cada año.

blocks.en: Is giving rising? Real, growing churches see their members’ giving climb year over year; a long flat line is a symptom.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Sube la ofrenda? Las iglesias reales y en crecimiento ven la ofrenda de sus miembros subir año tras año; una larga línea plana es un síntoma.

blocks.en: And the sharpest of all: What is the most exciting thing that has ever happened in the life of this church? If the honest answer lies fifteen years in the past, it is time to be afraid — for the church is now living on memory.
blocks.es_reference: Y la más aguda de todas: ¿Qué es lo más emocionante que ha pasado jamás en la vida de esta iglesia? Si la respuesta honesta está quince años en el pasado, es hora de temer — pues la iglesia ahora vive de la memoria.

blocks.en: Third, the marks of a growing church — the signs of vigor. Growing churches share a family resemblance. They have a clear, short vision — a sentence a member can actually repeat, not a paragraph no one remembers. They have a strong but humble pastor, a team-builder rather than a domineering boss, energetic and bold yet authentic, and committed to stay. They put people ahead of programs, asking of every activity the one ruthless question — how many lives has this actually changed? — and treating the program as expendable when the honest answer is “none.” They highlight prayer, teaching it and modeling it rather than merely mentioning it. Their evangelism is relational: they have largely abandoned the cold methods — the unwanted knock at the door, the intrusive phone call — for the slower power of friendship and the open door of the well-planned event. And they carry a sense of urgency, working as though the harvest will not wait, because it will not.
blocks.es_reference: Tercero, las marcas de una iglesia en crecimiento — las señales de vigor. Las iglesias en crecimiento comparten un aire de familia. Tienen una visión clara y corta — una frase que un miembro puede de veras repetir, no un párrafo que nadie recuerda. Tienen un pastor fuerte pero humilde, un constructor de equipo en vez de un jefe dominante, enérgico y audaz pero auténtico, y comprometido a permanecer. Ponen las personas antes que los programas, haciendo de cada actividad la única pregunta implacable — ¿cuántas vidas ha cambiado de veras esto? — y tratando el programa como prescindible cuando la respuesta honesta es "ninguna." Destacan la oración, enseñándola y modelándola en vez de solo mencionarla. Su evangelismo es relacional: han abandonado en gran parte los métodos fríos — el golpe no deseado a la puerta, la llamada telefónica intrusiva — por el poder más lento de la amistad y la puerta abierta del evento bien planeado. Y cargan un sentido de urgencia, trabajando como si la mies no fuera a esperar, porque no esperará.

blocks.en:
Set these three readings side by side and you will notice they are
not three lists but one examination. The vital signs tell you whether
there is life; the warning signs tell you whether that life is ebbing;
the marks of vigor tell you what life looks like at full strength. Run
them honestly on your own congregation — not on the church you wish you
led, but the one you actually do — and you will know, as a physician
knows, where to begin.
blocks.es_reference: Ponga estas tres lecturas lado a lado y notará que no son tres listas sino un examen. Las señales vitales le dicen si hay vida; las señales de advertencia le dicen si esa vida mengua; las marcas de vigor le dicen cómo se ve la vida en plena fuerza. Aplíquelas honestamente a su propia congregación — no a la iglesia que desearía dirigir, sino a la que de veras dirige — y sabrá, como sabe un médico, por dónde empezar.

blocks.en: Where We Are Now (2026)
blocks.es_reference: Dónde Estamos Ahora (2026)

blocks.en: The diagnosis still works, but a few of the instruments need recalibrating for our day. The old vital signs assumed a church measured by the seats filled on Sunday; now we must learn to count the orbit as well as the room — the people who watch, listen, serve, and belong through a screen as truly as through a pew. A congregation can be quietly reaching far more people than its sanctuary count suggests, and quietly losing them, too; the honest leader learns to read both.
blocks.es_reference: El diagnóstico aún funciona, pero algunos de los instrumentos necesitan recalibrarse para nuestros días. Las viejas señales vitales suponían una iglesia medida por los asientos llenos el domingo; ahora debemos aprender a contar la órbita además del salón — la gente que observa, escucha, sirve y pertenece por una pantalla tan de veras como por una banca. Una congregación puede estar alcanzando calladamente a mucha más gente de lo que sugiere el conteo de su santuario, y perdiéndola también calladamente; el líder honesto aprende a leer ambas.

blocks.en: Two of the old tests have only sharpened with age. The question when did you last start something new? turns out to be the single most reliable sign of life there is — the church that keeps starting new groups, new classes, new congregations is the church that keeps growing. And the mark of relational evangelism over the cold call has been wholly vindicated; the entire movement has turned from dragging people into the building toward going out to meet them where they live. The day of the unwanted knock and the cold phone call is simply over.
blocks.es_reference: Dos de las viejas pruebas solo se han afilado con la edad. La pregunta ¿cuándo inició algo nuevo por última vez? resulta ser la señal de vida más confiable que hay — la iglesia que sigue iniciando nuevos grupos, nuevas clases, nuevas congregaciones es la iglesia que sigue creciendo. Y la marca del evangelismo relacional por encima de la llamada fría ha sido vindicada del todo; todo el movimiento se ha vuelto de arrastrar a la gente al edificio hacia salir a encontrarla donde vive. El día del golpe no deseado y la llamada fría sencillamente terminó.

blocks.en: One test must be read in a new light. The old sign of health asked whether a church drew people from outside its own denomination. The deeper question now is whether a church is reaching anyone genuinely new at all, or merely trading sheep with the church down the road — and above all whether it is reaching back for the great company of the formerly churched, who are more open to a gracious invitation home than we feared. A church can post a healthy count and still be only rearranging the same believers; the truest sign of vigor is a name on the roll that belonged to no church at all a year ago.
blocks.es_reference: Una prueba debe leerse a una nueva luz. La vieja señal de salud preguntaba si una iglesia atraía gente de fuera de su propia denominación. La pregunta más profunda ahora es si una iglesia está alcanzando a alguien genuinamente nuevo en absoluto, o solo intercambiando ovejas con la iglesia de al lado — y sobre todo si está alcanzando de vuelta a la gran compañía de los que antes asistían, más abiertos a una invitación bondadosa a volver de lo que temíamos. Una iglesia puede mostrar un conteo sano y aun así solo estar reacomodando a los mismos creyentes; la señal más verdadera de vigor es un nombre en la lista que hace un año no pertenecía a ninguna iglesia.

blocks.en: And here a hard word must be added to the diagnosis of decline. We have learned that a church can carry the vital sign of a strong, visionary, long-tenured pastor and still come crashing down — when gift is not matched by character. So a thorough examination now asks not only whether the leadership is able but whether it is trustworthy, and whether a healthy circle of accountability surrounds the leader. We will give that its due in the next unit. The most pointed diagnostic question of our moment, though, is the old targeting question turned to the mirror: whom have we actually reached in the past twelve months? If the answer is only people exactly like ourselves, only the already-churched, only the aging — then the warning light is on, however full the room. The good news worth ending on is that the patient is not as far gone as the headlines suggest: after a long decline, attendance has begun, in many places, to rise again. The diagnosis is sober. It is not hopeless. And no church was ever healed by refusing to be examined.
blocks.es_reference: Y aquí debe añadirse una palabra dura al diagnóstico del declive. Hemos aprendido que una iglesia puede portar la señal vital de un pastor fuerte, visionario y de larga estancia y aun venirse abajo estrepitosamente — cuando el don no está a la altura del carácter. Así que un examen minucioso ahora pregunta no solo si el liderazgo es capaz sino si es confiable, y si un círculo sano de rendición de cuentas rodea al líder. Le daremos su lugar en la siguiente unidad. La pregunta diagnóstica más aguda de nuestro momento, sin embargo, es la vieja pregunta del enfoque vuelta al espejo: ¿a quién hemos alcanzado de veras en los últimos doce meses? Si la respuesta son solo personas exactamente como nosotros, solo los que ya asisten, solo los que envejecen — entonces la luz de advertencia está encendida, por lleno que esté el salón. La buena noticia con que vale la pena terminar es que el paciente no está tan grave como sugieren los titulares: tras un largo declive, la asistencia ha comenzado, en muchos lugares, a subir de nuevo. El diagnóstico es sobrio. No es desesperado. Y ninguna iglesia fue jamás sanada negándose a ser examinada.

fill.prompt: "Examine yourselves as to whether you are in the ____" (2 Corinthians 13:5).
What God counts is ____, not merely decisions.
The measure of a servant is finally ____, not yield, for the increase is God's to give.
One vital sign is a mobilized ____, a church convinced that every member has been gifted for ministry.
The three sizes are celebration, congregation, and the intimate, almost family-sized circle called the ____.
A church that has used the same rooms the same way for fifteen years is likely declining, for growth forces a church to keep reshaping its ____.
A warning question asks whether the church is accumulating ____ or consuming it.
If the most exciting thing in a church's life lies fifteen years in the past, the church is now living on ____.
Growing churches have a clear, short vision: a ____ a member can actually repeat, not a paragraph no one remembers.
The evangelism of growing churches is ____, trading the cold call for the slower power of friendship.

sa.prompt: Explain the diagnostic approach to a church using the physician image, and name the conviction that growth matters to God yet what He counts is disciples.
sa.model: Like a physician, a wise leader begins with diagnosis, not cure, honestly examining the church before reaching for any remedy. Growth matters to God, but what He counts is disciples, not mere decisions, real people brought into living fellowship with Christ. A church that refuses to examine itself is flying blind.

sa.prompt: List and explain the vital signs of a healthy church (the pulse).
sa.model: The vital signs are a pastor who wants to reach people, leads, and stays; a mobilized laity convinced every member is gifted for ministry and putting those gifts to work; and the right balance of three sizes, celebration in corporate worship, congregation in mid-sized groups, and cell in the intimate circle where life is shared. Where these are present, life is present.

sa.prompt: Give the warning signs of a plateau. State at least three of the pointed diagnostic questions.
sa.model: Warning signs include: how long since the church adapted its space, for fifteen years unchanged signals decline; when did you last start a new class, group, or ministry; are you accumulating capital or consuming it; is giving rising year over year; and the sharpest, what is the most exciting thing that has ever happened here, for if it lies fifteen years back the church lives on memory.

sa.prompt: Describe the marks of a growing church (the signs of vigor). Name at least four.
sa.model: Growing churches share a family resemblance: a clear short vision a member can repeat; a strong but humble pastor, a team-builder committed to stay; people ahead of programs, asking how many lives a program has changed; prayer taught and modeled, not merely mentioned; relational evangelism rather than cold calls; and a sense of urgency, working as though the harvest will not wait.

sa.prompt: Why must we now count the 'orbit' as well as the room? How does this change the old vital signs?
sa.model: The old vital signs assumed a church measured by Sunday seats; now we must count the orbit too, the people who watch, serve, and belong through a screen as truly as through a pew. A congregation can be reaching far more than its sanctuary count suggests, and quietly losing them as well, so the honest leader learns to read both the room and the orbit.

sa.prompt: Why is 'when did you last start something new?' the single most reliable sign of life, and how has relational evangelism been vindicated?
sa.model: The church that keeps starting new groups, classes, and congregations is the church that keeps growing, so when did you last start something new is the most reliable sign of life. And relational evangelism has been wholly vindicated; the whole movement has turned from dragging people into the building toward meeting them where they live. The day of the cold call is over.

sa.prompt: Explain the deeper version of the old 'reaching outside your denomination' test for our day.
sa.model: The old sign asked whether a church drew people from outside its denomination. The deeper question now is whether it reaches anyone genuinely new, or merely trades sheep with the church down the road, and above all whether it reaches the formerly churched, who are more open than we feared. A healthy count can be only rearranging the same believers.

sa.prompt: Why must a thorough diagnosis now ask whether leadership is trustworthy, not only able? Connect to accountability.
sa.model: We have learned that a church can have a gifted, visionary, long-tenured pastor and still collapse when gift is not matched by character. So a thorough diagnosis asks not only whether leadership is able but whether it is trustworthy, and whether a healthy circle of accountability surrounds the leader. The lone, unaccountable leader is the figure the years have taught us to fear.

sa.prompt: State the most pointed diagnostic question of our moment, and explain why a full room is not enough to answer it.
sa.model: The sharpest question turns the targeting principle to the mirror: whom have we actually reached in the past twelve months? If the answer is only people exactly like ourselves, only the aging, only the already-churched, the warning light is on however full the room. A full room can be people simply staying or being swapped, not anyone genuinely new being reached.

sa.prompt: Synthesis: Run the three readings (vital signs, warning signs, marks of vigor) on a church and show they form one examination, not three lists.
sa.model: The vital signs tell whether there is life; the warning signs tell whether that life is ebbing; the marks of vigor tell what life looks like at full strength. Together they are one examination, not three lists. Run honestly on the church you actually lead, not the one you wish you led, they tell you, as a physician knows, exactly where to begin.
